segments.text:
Container traffic at the Port of Eastmere stays below trend as services skip calls

*As of 2026-10-09; slice covers the trailing 24h to that date; 26 signals.*

**BLUF:** Eastmere throughput stays low, with skipped feeder calls and a closed northern berth keeping arrivals at minimal levels (signal:00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000a0)(signal:00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000a1)(signal:00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000a3).

## What changed

- No material change; throughput remained low as in the prior read of 8 October 2026 [27].

## Why it matters

- Skipped feeder calls and a berth closure point to continued capacity loss that deters carriers from scheduling calls (signal:00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000a0)(signal:00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000a3).
- Only seven container vessels called in a day, a direct sign of reduced throughput (signal:00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000a1).
- The regulator reaffirmed it will review berth allocation, which keeps rules uncertain for carriers (signal:00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000a5).

## What would change this

A sustained rise in weekly arrivals (more than 50 % of the earlier average) would overturn the assessment; this desk does not currently collect raw call data.

## Indicators

- Arrival volume drop: confirmed low calls (only seven vessels) (signal:00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000a1).
- Berth closure: dredging closure of the northern berth (signal:00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000a3).
- Major rerouting declared: not observed.
- Surcharge move: not observed.

question: Over the window, did container traffic through the Port of Eastmere recover, hold, or fall compared with the previous six weeks?
